items.question: My neighbour is ___ pilot.
explanations: ‘Pilot’ starts with a consonant sound (/p/), so ‘an’ doesn’t fit.
Correct! A job takes a/an, and ‘pilot’ starts with a consonant sound: ‘a pilot’.
A singular job needs a/an: ‘a pilot’.

items.question: I need ___ new phone; mine is broken.
explanations: ‘New’ starts with a consonant sound (/n/), so ‘an’ doesn’t fit.
‘Phone’ is singular and countable, so it needs an article.
Correct! Any new phone, and ‘new’ starts with a consonant sound: ‘a new phone’.

items.question: Could you give me ___ information about the course?
explanations: ‘Information’ is uncountable, so it can’t take ‘a’.
‘Information’ is uncountable, so it can’t take ‘an’.
Correct! Uncountable nouns take ‘some’ instead of a/an: ‘some information’.
‘One information’ doesn’t work; to count it, say ‘a piece of information’.

items.question: We have English lessons twice ___ week.
explanations: ‘Twice the week’ is a common slip; to mean ‘per’ we use ‘a’.
Correct! Here ‘a’ means ‘per’ (every): ‘twice a week’.
‘Week’ starts with a consonant sound (/w/), so ‘an’ doesn’t fit.
‘Twice week’ is missing the article that means ‘per’.

items.question: The twins have ___ brown eyes.
explanations: ‘Eyes’ is plural, so ‘a’ can’t go before it.
‘Eyes’ is plural, so ‘an’ can’t go before it.
Correct! A plural noun takes no a/an: ‘brown eyes’.

items.question: What ___ beautiful day!
explanations: Correct! In an exclamation with a singular noun we say ‘what a/an’: ‘What a beautiful day!’
In an exclamation with a singular noun we say ‘what a/an’, not ‘what the’.
‘Beautiful’ starts with a consonant sound (/b/), so ‘an’ doesn’t fit.
A singular countable noun after ‘what’ needs a/an.

items.question: He works as ___ electrician.
explanations: Correct! A job takes a/an, and ‘electrician’ starts with a vowel sound: ‘an electrician’.
‘Electrician’ starts with a vowel sound (/ɪ/), so ‘a’ doesn’t fit.
After ‘works as’, a singular job takes a/an.

items.question: Which sentence is correct?
explanations: Correct! ‘Advice’ is uncountable: ‘some advice’ (or ‘a piece of advice’).
‘Advice’ is uncountable, so it can’t take ‘an’; say ‘some advice’ or ‘a piece of advice’.
‘Advice’ is uncountable, so it can’t take a/an. And even with a countable noun, ‘advice’ starts with a vowel sound, so it would be ‘an’, not ‘a’.

items.question: We waited for about ___ hour.
explanations: Correct! ‘Hour’ has a silent h, so it starts with a vowel sound: ‘an hour’.
‘The hour’ would mean a particular hour we both know; here we only say how long.
‘Hour’ has a silent h, so it starts with a vowel sound; ‘a’ doesn’t fit.
‘Hour’ is singular and countable, so it needs an article.

items.question: Which is the correct way to say it?
explanations: We don’t put ‘a’ before ‘my’: say ‘my cousin’ or ‘a cousin of mine’.
Correct! With ‘my’ we don’t need a/an: ‘my cousin’.
‘Cousin’ is singular and countable, so it needs an article: ‘a cousin of mine’.
